title: Describe things, share preferences, and make plans

grammarPoints.title: Describe things with present-tense adjectives
grammarPoints.meaning: Use adjectives to say what something is like now or generally. Japanese has two adjective classes with different negative forms.
grammarPoints.formation: い-adjective + です; negative: replace final い with くないです. な-adjective base + です; negative: base + じゃないです.
notes: いい becomes よくない, including compounds built from いい; かわいい is regular.
きれい and きらい end in い but belong to the な class. Do not attach じゃない to an い-adjective.
とても / すごく / ちょっと can precede adjectives. あまり and ぜんぜん normally accompany a negative predicate.
忙しい describes a busy person; にぎやか describes a lively place.

grammarPoints.title: Describe how things were
grammarPoints.meaning: Put an adjective in the past when describing an earlier experience or state.
grammarPoints.formation: い-adjective: final い → かったです / くなかったです. な-adjective: base + でした / じゃなかったです.
notes: Keep です unchanged after the past form of an い-adjective; 高いでした is incorrect.
いい becomes よかった / よくなかった.
More formal negatives such as 高くありませんでした and 静かではありませんでした are also possible.

grammarPoints.title: Put an adjective before a noun
grammarPoints.meaning: An adjective can identify or describe the noun immediately after it.
grammarPoints.formation: い-adjective dictionary form + noun; な-adjective base + な + noun.
notes: Do not put です between the adjective and noun.
The adjective must describe the noun naturally: prices and age suit belongings, while quiet or lively can describe settings.

grammarPoints.title: Express likes and dislikes
grammarPoints.meaning: 好き and きらい describe feelings about a thing or person. 大好き and 大きらい express stronger feelings.
grammarPoints.formation: Person は thing が 好き / きらい です. Treat these words as な-adjectives; before a noun use 好きな / きらいな.
notes: The liked thing normally takes が, not を. Use は when explicitly contrasting it with another thing.
A milder dislike can be expressed as あまり好きじゃないです.
私の好きな本 means a book I like; の marks the person here. Neutral 好きでもきらいでもないです means neither like nor dislike.
Use the noun version of an activity here; verb + の is introduced in Lesson 8.

grammarPoints.title: Suggest a shared activity
grammarPoints.meaning: Use ましょう to suggest doing something together or accept a plan. ましょうか asks whether to do it together.
grammarPoints.formation: Remove ます from a polite verb and add ましょう or ましょうか.
notes: The context must include both speaker and listener in the proposed activity.
An invitation with ませんか is gentler; ましょう often follows agreement to a plan.
Lesson 6 introduces ましょうか for an offer to act on someone else’s behalf.

grammarPoints.title: Count flat objects
grammarPoints.meaning: Japanese uses counters matched to what is counted. 枚 counts thin, flat things such as sheets, photos, or shirts.
grammarPoints.formation: Object を number + 枚 + verb. The quantity usually follows the noun and its particle.
notes: Do not use 枚 for people, bound books, or arbitrary objects.
Numbers do not need a particle when used as quantities before the verb. Ask 何枚 for how many flat objects.
